newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Alcopops take fizz out of Matthew Clark.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Alcopops take fizz out of Matthew Clark.

text.p: British drinks firm Matthew Clark Plc stunned the stock market with a profits warning on Monday because of tough competition from new alcopop' drinks, leading investment houses to gear up to downgrade profit estimates.

"This was really quite a shock...almost every broker in London was a buyer of this stock and everyone had a tight range in expectations. We're going to see some pretty hefty downgrades this week," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

Shares in cider maker Matthew Clark slumped over 30 percent after the company said the growth of alcopop drinks hit summer sales of its Diamond White cider, K and Babycham brands -- key pillars of profits at the branded drinks division.
A flood of cheap cider products had also swallowed market growth and swamped profit margins, the company said.
"Whilst it is too early to assess the impact on the full year performance, current estimates indicate the above factors will materially affect results," Matthew Clark warned.
Matthew Clark shares were down 219-1/2 at 450-1/2 following the warning.

Alcoholic lemonades and similar alcoholic long drinks have made significant inroads into the British market, which research body Euromonitor said in May would be worth almost 170 million pounds ($264 million) this year after 100 million in 1995.
The alcopops, particularly popular with female and young drinkers, have unleashed a storm of controversy over whether they encourage under-age drinking.

Drinks industry leaders agreed in January to a voluntary code of practice to try to prevent promoting the drinks to under-age drinkers or linking their consumption with sexual prowess, drugs or violence.
Leading products include Hooper's Hooch alcoholic lemonade and Two Dogs, marketed by Merrydown. Analysts said Matthew Clark would have its work cut out to recoup lost markets and pull back consumers.
"They appear to have lost enormous volume in three key brands and it doesn't look hopeful for the full year," a second analyst said.
Tuesday's stock market rout echoes similar problems two months ago Matthew Clark stunned investors with weaker than expected profits for the year.
The weakness spread to other drinks companies, notably, Bulmer HP Holdings lost 50p to a low of 530p before recovering somewhat to 552-1/2, while Guinness shed 4p to 470. ($1=.6436 Pound)
